events.title: Mutiny on the Bounty
events.description: Fletcher Christian led a mutiny aboard HMS Bounty in the South Pacific. Lieutenant William Bligh and 18 loyal sailors were cast adrift in an open boat. Bligh's party reached the island of Tofua, while Christian sailed on to Tonga.
events.significance: The mutiny became one of history's most famous naval revolts. Bligh's epic open-boat voyage is still celebrated as a feat of navigation and survival.

events.title: Farragut Captures New Orleans
events.description: During the American Civil War, Admiral David Farragut's Union fleet captured New Orleans, the largest city in the Confederacy, after running past the forts that guarded the Mississippi River.
events.significance: The Confederacy lost its largest city and its most important port. The Union gained control of the lower Mississippi, a major step toward its eventual victory.

events.title: Death of Benito Mussolini
events.description: Benito Mussolini, the Italian Fascist dictator who had ruled Italy for more than two decades, was killed in the final days of World War II in Europe.
events.significance: His death marked the end of Italian Fascism. It came just days before Germany's surrender.

events.title: Charles de Gaulle Resigns
events.description: Charles de Gaulle, the first president of France's Fifth Republic, resigned after voters rejected his proposed reforms in a nationwide referendum.
events.significance: The resignation ended the career of the wartime leader who had shaped postwar France. It closed an era in French politics.

events.title: The First Space Tourist
events.description: American millionaire Dennis Tito became the world's first paying space tourist when he reached the International Space Station.
events.significance: Tito's trip opened the door to commercial human spaceflight. It showed that private citizens could travel to orbit.
